newsitem.title: USA: ITT to split into three to thwart Hilton bid.
newsitem.headline: ITT to split into three to thwart Hilton bid.

text.p: Hotel and casino giant ITT Corp. launched a massive restructuring plan on Wednesday to thwart a $6.5 billion hostile bid from rival Hilton Hotels Corp. by splitting into three companies and buying back $2.1 billion in stock.

Under the long-awaited plan, ITT would split into a hotel and casino company, to be called ITT Destinations; ITT Corp., which will publish telephone directories, and ITT Educational Services Inc., which will run technical schools.
Following the news, ITT's stock jumped $4.875 to $67.50, while Hilton edged up 18.75 cents to $29.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Hilton wants to acquire 50.1 percent of ITT's stock at $55 a share.
ITT, which owns the Sheraton brand hotels and Caesars brand casinos, has rejected the bid and is refocusing its strategy on core hotel and gambling assets.

"Separating our lodging and gaming operations from ITT's other remaining assets is in keeping with our goal of creating current value for ITT shareholders while enhancing the long-term prospects and strategic opportunities for each business," said Rand Araskog, ITT chairman and chief executive.
Hilton responded by calling the spin-off plan a "smoke-and-mirrors scheme" that would be "value destructive" and said a combination of ITT with Hilton would create greater value.

Under the plan, ITT stockholders will keep their ITT shares, which will represent ownership in the telephone directories business. For each share they hold, they will receive one new share in the hotel and casino company ITT Destinations, and about 0.25 share of ITT Educational Services.

Araskog will become chairman and CEO of ITT Destinations, which will focus on its Sheraton hotels and Caesars casinos. The company will have 424 hotels in 62 countries and casinos in Las Vegas, Atlantic City and other major gaming centres.

The company also reported sharply higher earnings for the second quarter of $199 million, or $1.69 a share, on revenues of $1.72 billion, vs. year-earlier earnings of $96 million, or 81 cents a share, on revenues of $1.69 billion.
ITT said it would spend $2.1 billion to repurchase 30 million of its common shares at $70 each, or about 26 percent of its outstanding shares.
Also, the company said it plans to buy back the entire $2.0 billion of existing ITT debt through a tender offer later in the year.
In approving the pact, ITT's board of directors again voted unanimously to recommend that shareholders reject Hilton's tender offer.
ITT said it intends for the three-way split to be tax-free.

"Hilton cannot execute our plan because it could not do a tax-free spinoff of World Directories and ESI (ITT Educational Services) for five years, and it would have to pay at least $500 million in taxes if it carried out its promise to sell these assets, which have a very low tax basis," Araskog said.
ITT said it has agreed, after the split, to sell a 32.9 percent stake in the telephone directories company to the New York investment firm Clayton Dubilier & Rice Inc. for $225 million in cash.

Clayton Dubilier will also get 10-year warrants to buy common stock in the directories company at a 50 percent premium to its initial purchase price. If the warrants are exercised, Clayton Dubilier will own a 46.6 percent stake in the company.
The new ITT Corp.'s sole asset will be 100 percent of ITT World Directories Inc.
ITT said it recently bought the 20 percent of World Directories it did not own from BellSouth Corp. for $254 million in cash.
In a separate transaction last week, ITT World Directories declared and paid an $11 million dividend to BellSouth, ITT said.
Following the transaction with Clayton Dubilier, World Directories will have $1.05 billion in debt, giving it an initial total enterprise value of $1.7 billion, ITT said.
